 dict(id="ENV-01", cat="Environmental", sev="Critical",
  title="Grand Junction HQ: uninsured chlorinated-solvent (DNAPL) and petroleum contamination, uninvestigated since 2019",
  finding=("The June 2019 Phase II ESA found PCE/TCE (DNAPL) and petroleum/BTEX contamination in soil and groundwater above Colorado "
           "standards. It also found soil-gas exceedances indicating a potential vapor-intrusion pathway into a maintenance building "
           "occupied daily by RES employees ('a matter warranting prompt attention'). There are no off-site sentinel wells, so plume "
           "containment is 'preliminary,' and groundwater flows northwest toward the Colorado River. The 2006 UST closure file remains "
           "open with no NFA letter. None of the recommended follow-up (off-site wells, vapor intrusion assessment, VCUP entry, update "
           "before any transaction or financing) has been done in more than five years. The $1.83M-$2.67M estimate is in 2019 dollars "
           "and excludes vapor-intrusion mitigation, off-site remediation, third-party claims and NRD. Only $2.2M of the $3.2M accrual "
           "relates to Grand Junction. As current owner, RES is liable under CERCLA regardless of fault. Because this is an "
           "RCRA-permitted facility, the December 31, 2026 permit renewal could bring facility-wide corrective action. The PLL "
           "policy excludes gradual contamination at owned sites. The Permit Schedule mis-describes the contamination location and "
           "migration direction relative to the Phase II."),
  sources="ESA ss.2-8; EPS s.2.1, s.5; LIT s.VI.A; RPL s.2.1; INS s.4; CAS s.3, s.10",
  exposure="2019 estimate $1.83M-$2.67M; illustrative ~30% cost escalation gives up to ~$3.5M before vapor intrusion, off-site and DNAPL contingencies. Accrual covers $2.2M. Lender EoD if a remediation order exceeds $1M.",
  lo=1830000, hi=3471000,
  impact="Special indemnity; dedicated escrow; price; pre-signing investigation",
  action=("Commission an updated Phase I/II with off-site downgradient wells and a vapor-intrusion assessment (sub-slab and indoor air) "
          "before signing. Address worker exposure immediately. SPA: uncapped or separately capped specific environmental indemnity "
          "for pre-closing conditions at Grand Junction, surviving at least 6 years, backed by a dedicated environmental escrow sized "
          "to the updated estimate. Evaluate VCUP entry and Colorado Petroleum Storage Tank Fund eligibility for the UST release. Bind "
          "a site pollution policy covering known conditions if the market permits."),
  requests="Full 180-page Phase II and the 2018 Phase I; all groundwater monitoring data since 2019; UST closure file; CDPHE correspondence; accrual workpapers."),

 dict(id="ENV-02", cat="Environmental", sev="High",

  finding=("The NOV (July 18, 2024) alleges ~14,000 gallons of F001/F002 listed spent solvents were stored in an unpermitted staging area "
           "beyond the 90-day period. The CIM calls it a self-reported 'storage duration exceedance' that is 'within the scope of normal "
           "operations,' and the Permit Schedule describes a satellite-accumulation exceedance of the 55-gallon limit. The parties dispute "
           "12 versus 31 days ($450K versus $1,162,500 at the $37,500/day figure management uses, which is an outdated per-day "
           "maximum). Management's settlement estimate is $200K-$450K, and nothing is accrued. Seller's counsel cites 'no prior RCRA "
           "violations,' while the Permit Schedule notes a 2016 violation. The compliance record will matter for the 2026 Part B renewal. "
           "Post-signing, LOI s.9(e) requires Buyer consent for settlements over $100K."),
  sources="LIT s.III.A; EPS s.2.1, s.6; CIM s.IX.A; LOI s.5.5, s.9(e); CAS s.6, s.12",
  exposure="$200K (management low) to $1.16M+ (CDPHE position), plus possible injunctive/compliance-order costs.",
  lo=200000, hi=1162500,
  impact="Special indemnity; Net Debt/accrual",
  action=("Obtain the NOV, the September 5, 2024 response and the inspection report. Treat the CDPHE penalty as a specific indemnity (or "
          "an indebtedness item at the CDPHE number) outside the basket and cap. Require Buyer approval rights over settlement and over "
          "any compliance order."),
  requests="NOV; inspection report; RES response and exhibits; any CDPHE settlement communications; corrective-action documentation."),

 dict(id="ENV-03", cat="Environmental", sev="High",
  title="Wyoming (Casper) hazardous waste permit expired November 30, 2024; 'timely renewal' status is unverified",
  finding=("Permit WY-HW-2019-033 expired November 30, 2024, and the renewal application was filed October 15, 2024, only 46 days before "
           "expiration. Under the federal RCRA permitting framework generally adopted by authorized states, a renewal application is "
           "due at least 180 days before expiration (40 C.F.R. s.270.10(h)), and continuation of an expired permit depends on a timely "
           "and complete application (s.270.51). Unless Wyoming rules or a DEQ extension provide otherwise, Casper (68 FTEs; Wyoming "
           "revenue $30.2M, or 23.7% of the total) may be operating without valid authorization. Non-renewal of a material permit is "
           "also a credit agreement Event of Default. The CIM describes the filing as timely without qualification."),
  sources="EPS s.2.4; CIM s.III, s.V.C; RPL s.4.3; CCS 'Customer Concentration Summary' (geography); CAS s.10",
  exposure="Interruption or penalties at a facility serving ~$30M of revenue; permit-renewal conditions.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Closing condition; special indemnity",
  action=("Obtain the renewal application, DEQ completeness determination and any written confirmation of continued authorization. "
          "Engage Wyoming environmental counsel. Closing condition: renewed permit issued, or written DEQ confirmation that the "
          "facility is authorized to operate pending renewal."),
  requests="Renewal application (Oct 15, 2024); DEQ correspondence; prior permit conditions; 2022 inspection report."),

toolu_011aRxBetu7FCD7z4wssQTGC.content:
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Shared red-flag data for Project Ridgeline memo and tracker."""

CIM = "CIM"
LOI = "Executed LOI"
CAS = "Credit Agreement Summary"
CCS = "Customer Contract Summary (xlsx)"
EBS = "Employee Census & Benefits Summary"
EAS = "Employment Agreements Summary"
EPS = "Environmental Permit Schedule"
INS = "Insurance Program Summary"
LIT = "Litigation & Regulatory Summary"
ORG = "Org Chart & Equity Structure"
ESA = "Phase II ESA Executive Summary"
QOE = "QoE Data Request Response (xlsx)"
RPL = "Real Property & Lease Schedule"

# Each flag: id, cat, title, sev, finding, sources, exposure, lo, hi, impact, action, requests
FLAGS = [
 dict(id="FIN-01", cat="Financial / Quality of Earnings", sev="Critical",
  title="Adjusted EBITDA underpinning the LOI valuation is unreconciled and internally inconsistent",
  finding=("The LOI prices the deal at 8.0x-9.0x FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA of $22.8M (EV $182M-$205M). The CIM bridges $18.4M "
           "reported EBITDA to $22.8M with ~$4.4M of add-backs; the QoE EBITDA Bridge shows $5.4M of add-backs and $23.8M "
           "Adjusted EBITDA, and management states that the $1.0M difference has not been identified. Separately, the QoE "
           "Historical P&L shows FY2024 EBIT of $18,400K and a 'Reported EBITDA' line of $26,036K (EBIT plus $7,636K D&A), while "
           "pre-tax income is derived directly from EBIT without any D&A deduction. The $18.4M figure management calls "
           "'reported EBITDA' therefore appears to be EBIT, or the P&L omits D&A; either way the starting point of the bridge "
           "cannot be tied to the financial statements."),
  sources="LOI s.3.1; CIM s.II, s.VI.A-B; QoE 'Historical P&L' and 'EBITDA Bridge' tabs (reconciliation note); CAS s.4",
  exposure="Valuation: each $1.0M of EBITDA = $8.0M-$9.0M of EV at the LOI multiple range.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Price; QoE scope; signing condition",
  action=("Do not finalize price until Bridgewater Forsyth completes a full QoE tied to audited trial balances, including proof of "
          "revenue and proof of cash. Require management to deliver a single reconciled FY2022-FY2024 EBITDA bridge to the GL. Re-base "
          "price on diligence-adjusted EBITDA (see FIN-02/FIN-03). SPA: financial statements rep (GAAP, no undisclosed "
          "liabilities) as a fundamental-style rep with extended survival; specific indemnity for EBITDA-bridge misstatement is "
          "not customary, so price protection is the primary remedy."),
  requests="Trial balances and GL detail FY2022-FY2024; management EBITDA bridge reconciled to audited/reviewed statements; D&A schedule; explanation of the $1.0M CIM vs. QoE difference."),

 dict(id="FIN-02", cat="Financial / Quality of Earnings", sev="Critical",
  title="$1.2M 'one-time litigation settlement' add-back is described three different ways and may be a gain, not a cost",
  finding=("(i) The CIM says RES 'incurred costs' for a litigation settlement 'resolved during the period.' (ii) The QoE bridge and P&L "
           "describe a $1.2M cash payment by RES to settle the Harper Environmental matter (Mesa County Case No. 2023-CV-1847) "
           "in July 2024 for breach of an exclusivity clause. (iii) Seller's counsel's Litigation Summary states that Harper is still "
           "pending (discovery; mediation set for February 2025; RES is the plaintiff seeking $2.1M) and that the $1.2M relates to "
           "the Clearwater Logistics matter, in which Clearwater PAID RES a net $1.2M (received April 2024). If the Litigation "
           "Summary is correct, the add-back runs the wrong way: a non-recurring gain should be deducted, not added back."),
  sources="CIM s.VI.B; QoE 'Historical P&L' (Litigation Settlement (Harper) line) and 'EBITDA Bridge'; LIT s.II.A, s.III.A, s.IV.A",
  exposure="EBITDA overstatement of $1.2M (add-back removed) to $2.4M (add-back removed and gain eliminated); EV impact ~$9.6M-$21.6M at 8.0x-9.0x.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Price; credibility of management financial reporting",
  action=("Obtain the Clearwater settlement agreement, Harper docket and the GL entries for the $1.2M. Remove the add-back in all "
          "valuation cases; if the Clearwater receipt sits in reported EBITDA, deduct it. Escalate as a management credibility "
          "issue with Greylock Merritt."),
  requests="Clearwater settlement agreement and cash receipt; Harper pleadings/docket; GL coding of the $1.2M; FY2024 'other income' detail."),

 dict(id="FIN-03", cat="Financial / Quality of Earnings", sev="High",
  title="Other add-backs (integration, ERP, owner compensation, asbestos wind-down) are recurring, unsupported or conditional",
  finding=("Pinnacle integration costs have been added back for three consecutive years ($1,240K / $620K / $800K, FY2022-FY2024), "
           "2.5 years after the March 2022 closing, while the CIM calls integration 'substantially complete.' ERP costs ($385K FY2023; "
           "$650K FY2024) relate to a 'RidgeTrack Phase 2 upgrade' expected to finish in Q2 FY2025, contrary to the CIM statement "
           "that the system is fully operational with no further spend. The $950K owner-compensation normalization assumes the "
           "Calloways' $875K salaries fall to $400K each based on a benchmarking study by Bridgewater Forsyth Group (the buyer's own "
           "QoE provider, which raises independence and circularity concerns); it is only valid if new post-closing employment "
           "agreements actually reset pay, and the CIM says both founders will continue. Asbestos wind-down costs appear in FY2023 "
           "($920K) and FY2024 ($1.8M) and exclude long-tail liabilities (ENV-05)."),
  sources="QoE 'EBITDA Bridge', 'Executive Compensation'; CIM s.VI.B, s.XII.C; EAS s.3-4",
  exposure="Base-case disallowance of integration ($0.80M) and ERP ($0.65M) = $1.45M EBITDA (~$11.6M-$13.1M EV). Owner-comp add-back ($0.95M) at risk if post-closing pay is not reset.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Price; post-closing employment terms",
  action=("Treat integration and ERP/RidgeTrack costs as recurring in the base case. Accept the owner-comp add-back only if executed "
          "new employment agreements at market pay are a signing deliverable (LOI s.8(g)). Commission an independent compensation benchmark."),
  requests="Invoices and project trackers for integration/ERP spend; Infor contract; Bridgewater Forsyth compensation study and engagement terms; proposed post-closing comp for the Calloways."),

 dict(id="FIN-04", cat="Financial / Quality of Earnings", sev="Critical",
  title="Earnings are declining, a trend omitted from the CIM",
  finding=("The QoE shows Management Adjusted EBITDA of $28.1M in FY2023 versus $23.8M in FY2024 (down ~15%), with adjusted margin falling "
           "from 24.5% to 18.7%; 'reported' EBITDA fell 27% and net income fell 1.1% despite 11.1% revenue growth. Revenue growth has slowed "
           "each year (20.1%, 19.0%, 17.2%, 11.1%). The CIM shows no EBITDA for FY2020-FY2023 (dashes) and describes 'consistent, strong "
           "financial performance.' Combined with the DOE ceiling problem (REV-01), FY2025 run-rate EBITDA may be materially below FY2024."),
  sources="QoE 'Historical P&L' memo lines and 'EBITDA Bridge' (FY2022-FY2024); CIM s.VI.A",
  exposure="Valuation and MAC/forecast risk; buyer is paying a growth multiple for a business whose earnings are contracting.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Price; structure (consider earn-out or seller note); financing",
  action=("Require monthly FY2024 and FY2025 YTD results and a management forecast with a DOE bridge. Consider pricing on a FY2025 "
          "run-rate basis or bridging the valuation gap with an earn-out or deferred consideration."),
  requests="Monthly P&L FY2023 to date; FY2025 budget (also a lender deliverable); backlog report by customer."),

 dict(id="FIN-05", cat="Financial / Quality of Earnings", sev="Critical",
  title="Audit status is contradictory, which bears on the LOI closing condition and the credit agreement",
  finding=("The CIM says the financial statements 'have not been audited' and are only reviewed by Hansen & Whitfield, CPAs. The QoE cover "
           "says FY2020-FY2023 were audited by Plante Moran PLLC and FY2024 is reviewed (unaudited). The Litigation Summary refers to a "
           "footnote 'in the FY2024 audited financial statements.' The credit agreement requires audited annual statements with an "
           "unqualified opinion within 120 days of each September 30 year-end, and LOI s.8(i) makes audited FY2022-FY2024 statements a "
           "closing condition. Plante Moran is also listed as Pinnacle acquisition accountant, which raises an auditor-independence question."),
  sources="CIM s.I, s.VI.A; QoE 'Cover & Instructions', 'EBITDA Bridge' (Pinnacle line); LIT s.II.B; CAS s.6, s.12; LOI s.8(i)",
  exposure="If audits were not performed: existing credit agreement reporting default and misrepresentation risk; closing timeline at risk (a FY2022-FY2024 audit cannot be completed by the February 14, 2025 target signing).",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Closing condition; timeline; reliance",
  action=("Obtain audit reports, engagement letters and management letters for every year. If FY2024 is unaudited, require an audit "
          "before signing or as a signing deliverable. Confirm what was delivered to HPNB under the reporting covenants."),
  requests="Audit opinions FY2020-FY2024; auditor engagement letters and management letters; compliance certificates and annual deliveries to HPNB."),

 dict(id="FIN-06", cat="Financial / Quality of Earnings", sev="High",
  title="Historical revenue, margins, service-line mix and geographic revenue differ across data room documents",
  finding=("FY2021/FY2022/FY2023 revenue is $82.1M/$97.6M/$114.8M (CIM), $82.15M/$97.8M/$114.6M (QoE) and $78.9M/$98.2M/$115.7M "
           "(Customer Contract Summary). Gross margin is 33.8%-35.0% (CIM) versus 35.0%-36.0% (QoE). The FY2024 service-line mix is "
           "45/25/18/12 (remediation/waste/emergency response/industrial cleaning) in the CIM and QoE, but 41.5/21.1/15.2/22.3 in the "
           "Customer Contract Summary. Geographic revenue allocates 100% of revenue to CO, WY and UT, with nothing to Montana or Idaho, "
           "even though the Company has a permitted Billings facility (44 FTEs), Helena, Missoula and Idaho operations and a Montana DEQ customer."),
  sources="CIM s.VI.A, s.IV.D; QoE 'Historical P&L', 'Service Line Detail'; CCS 'Historical Revenue by Customer', 'Customer Concentration Summary'; EBS s.2",
  exposure="Revenue integrity; NWC target and forecasting reliability.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="QoE scope; price",
  action="Expand QoE to include proof of revenue by customer, service line and state, and reconcile to sales-tax filings and state apportionment.",
  requests="Revenue by customer x service line x state FY2022-FY2024; state income tax apportionment workpapers."),

 dict(id="FIN-07", cat="Financial / Quality of Earnings", sev="High",
  title="Fleet underinvestment: maintenance capex is understated and there is a ~$9.8M replacement backlog",
  finding=("38 of 85 fleet/equipment units (44.7%) are at or past their stated useful life, many marked 'Replacement Deferred'. Average "
           "fleet age is 8.2 years against a 7-year life. Replacement cost of past-life units is $9.8M, against total NBV of only $1.24M. "
           "The QoE itself implies ~$3.3M a year of catch-up capex over three years, on top of the run-rate. Management's 'normalized' "
           "maintenance capex of $4.0M-$4.5M reflects suppressed FY2022-FY2023 spending ($4.0M/$3.55M). The fleet schedule also does not "
           "match the auto policy: 85 units (55 heavy trucks, 15 trailers, 15 pieces of heavy equipment) versus 87 insured vehicles "
           "(34 hazardous waste transport, 53 light-duty)."),
  sources="QoE 'Capex Detail', 'Fleet & Equipment Schedule'; CIM s.VI.C; INS s.3",
  exposure="$3.3M (one year of catch-up) to $9.8M (full backlog) of deferred capex; free-cash-flow and DOT/safety risk; possible uninsured units.",
  lo=3300000, hi=9800000,
  impact="Price (debt-like item or EV reduction); NWC/capex covenant",
  action=("Treat the deferred-capex backlog as a debt-like item or a price reduction. Commission a fleet condition and DOT compliance "
          "inspection. Reconcile the fleet register to the auto schedule and MCS-90 filings. Add an interim covenant requiring "
          "budgeted capex through closing."),
  requests="Fixed asset register; DOT inspection/out-of-service records; auto policy vehicle schedule; capital lease schedule."),

 dict(id="REV-01", cat="Revenue / Customers / Government Contracts", sev="Critical",
  title="DOE IDIQ (19.2% of revenue): ceiling nearly exhausted and reported DOE revenue cannot be reconciled to the task orders",
  finding=("Contract DE-EM-0005523 has a $45.0M ceiling and runs to August 31, 2026 with no option periods. Task-order data show $38.2M of TO "
           "ceilings issued, $31.7M of revenue recognized and $6.5M of TO backlog. Completed TOs were billed at full ceiling, so the "
           "claim that only $32.7M is 'obligated' (leaving $12.3M of ceiling) is inconsistent with the TO data; remaining ceiling may "
           "be as little as ~$6.8M. Even on management's figures the ceiling runs out around April-May 2025, at least 16 months before "
           "contract expiry (FY2025 revenue headwind of at least $12.1M, or 9.5% of revenue). Separately, DOE revenue reported for "
           "FY2021-FY2024 totals $63.9M (Customer Contract Summary) or $62.7M (QoE). That is roughly twice the $31.7M recognized under "
           "the IDIQ and exceeds the entire $45M ceiling, which means either undisclosed DOE contracts exist or DOE revenue is "
           "overstated. Clause H-12 requires written notice to the Contracting Officer within 30 days of a change in ownership; "
           "failure 'may be grounds for termination for default.' The Government can also terminate for convenience (FAR 52.249-2), "
           "and the most recent CPARS rating has slipped to 'Satisfactory' (TO -0008)."),
  sources="CCS 'Top 20 Customers' row 1, 'Historical Revenue by Customer', 'DOE IDIQ Utilization Analysis'; QoE 'Revenue by Customer'; CIM s.III, s.VI.D, s.VIII.A; LOI s.7.1(e)",
  exposure="FY2025 revenue headwind of at least $12.1M; at the ~37% remediation contribution margin, roughly $4.5M of EBITDA (~$36M-$40M EV). The revenue-integrity issue could be larger.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Price; walk-right; special condition",
  action=("Before signing: obtain the IDIQ contract, all modifications and TOs, funding/obligation records, invoices and DOE payment "
          "data (e.g., IPP/USAspending), and reconcile DOE revenue to them. Determine whether a ceiling increase or a follow-on vehicle "
          "is realistic and on what timetable. Confirm small-business size status and any recertification triggered by the "
          "acquisition (FAR 52.219-28), if the award was set aside. Closing deliverable: H-12 notice plan; consider a CO "
          "acknowledgment. Price on DOE-adjusted run-rate or use an earn-out tied to a ceiling increase or follow-on award."),
  requests="DE-EM-0005523 basic contract, all mods, all TOs and funding docs; CPARS reports; DOE invoices and receipts FY2021-FY2024; list of all other federal contracts; SAM/size representations."),

 dict(id="REV-02", cat="Revenue / Customers / Government Contracts", sev="Critical",
  title="Two irreconcilable customer rosters both total $127.3M",
  finding=("Other than DOE and CMMC, the top-20 customer list in the Customer Contract Summary (e.g., Western Slope Municipal Water District, "
           "High Plains Energy Partners, Intermountain Health Systems, Wasatch Front Petroleum, Silver Creek Mining) does not match the "
           "QoE 'Revenue by Customer' tab (e.g., Western Slope Energy Partners, Rio Tinto Kennecott, Suncor, Freeport-McMoRan, Marathon, "
           "Newmont, Chevron). Yet both total $127.3M and both show top-10 concentration of exactly 67.0%. The CIM's Customers C/D/E "
           "($10.2M/$7.6M/$6.4M) match neither. In the Customer Contract Summary, a $0.2M customer is ranked #10 ahead of a $4.1M customer "
           "(the true top-10 share is $89.2M, or 70.1%). 'All other' revenue is $13.8M (~85 customers), $19.1M (~120 accounts) or "
           "$42.0M (33%), depending on the document."),
  sources="CCS 'Top 20 Customers', 'Customer Concentration Summary'; QoE 'Revenue by Customer'; CIM s.VI.D",
  exposure="Fundamental revenue-existence/attribution risk; possible misrepresentation. Not quantifiable until revenue is proven.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Walk-right / signing condition; fraud carve-out",
  action=("Require customer-level revenue from the GL, tied to invoices, cash receipts and AR aging, with third-party confirmations for "
          "the top 20 under both lists. Consider forensic accounting procedures. SPA: fraud carve-out, no anti-sandbagging limitation, "
          "and a customer-list representation."),
  requests="Customer master file; revenue by customer from GL FY2022-FY2024; AR aging; cash receipts; executed contracts for both rosters."),

 dict(id="REV-03", cat="Revenue / Customers / Government Contracts", sev="High",
  title="Customer concentration and short-notice terminability, with many renewals falling in the signing-to-closing window",
  finding=("Top 5 customers account for 50.4% of revenue and the top 10 for 67%-70%. 12 of the top 20 contracts are terminable for "
           "convenience on 60 days' notice or less, and most MSAs have no minimum volumes. Terms expiring or renewing in the deal "
           "window include Silver Creek (Jan 14, 2025), Powder River (Jan 31, 2025), Piceance (Feb 28, 2025), High Plains Energy "
           "(Mar 14, 2025), Wasatch Front (Mar 31, 2025), Teton Steel (Apr 30, 2025), CMMC (May 31, 2025; 60-day non-renewal right) and "
           "Intermountain Health (expires June 30, 2025; renewal decision by February 2025; consent to assign and 60-day advance "
           "change-of-control notice). Elk Mountain ($3.2M) is a one-off 18-month project ending July 2025. The CIM nonetheless "
           "presents 67% top-10 concentration as strong diversification."),
  sources="CCS 'Top 20 Customers', 'Customer Concentration Summary'; CIM s.III, s.XIII",
  exposure="Revenue at risk from non-renewal or termination; Elk Mountain revenue is non-recurring ($3.2M).",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Price; interim covenants; closing deliverables",
  action=("Hold customer calls with the top 10 (with seller consent) before signing. Interim covenant and bring-down on material "
          "customer losses. Make Intermountain and other consent/notice items closing deliverables. Remove one-off project revenue "
          "from run-rate."),
  requests="All top-20 contracts and amendments; renewal/notice correspondence; backlog by customer."),

 dict(id="REV-04", cat="Revenue / Customers / Government Contracts", sev="Medium",
  title="Third-party consents and notices are required under customer contracts",
  finding=("8 of the top 20 customer contracts contain assignment, change-of-control or notification provisions: DOE (H-12 notice), "
           "Intermountain (consent; 60-day CoC notice), Utah DEQ (notice within 30 days; termination right if qualifications are "
           "affected), Rocky Mountain Pipeline (CoC triggers 30-day notice and consent period), CDOT (notice; consent for assignment), "
           "Summit County (board approval for any CoC), Frontier E&P (notice within 30 days) and Bridger Valley/Teton (mutual consent "
           "to assign). Pinnacle-legacy contracts are said to have been 'assumed by RES,' and whether those assignments were effective "
           "is unverified."),
  sources="CCS 'Top 20 Customers', 'Customer Concentration Summary'",
  exposure="Termination or leverage risk on ~$40M+ of revenue subject to notice/consent provisions.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Closing deliverables",
  action="Build a consent and notice plan (see 'Consents & Notices' tab). Make Summit County, Rocky Mountain Pipeline and Intermountain consents closing conditions or deliverables. Confirm the Pinnacle contract assignments.",
  requests="Assignment/assumption documents for Pinnacle-legacy contracts (PWS- references)."),

 dict(id="ENV-01", cat="Environmental", sev="Critical",
  title="Grand Junction HQ: uninsured chlorinated-solvent (DNAPL) and petroleum contamination, uninvestigated since 2019",
  finding=("The June 2019 Phase II ESA found PCE/TCE (DNAPL) and petroleum/BTEX contamination in soil and groundwater above Colorado "
           "standards. It also found soil-gas exceedances indicating a potential vapor-intrusion pathway into a maintenance building "
           "occupied daily by RES employees ('a matter warranting prompt attention'). There are no off-site sentinel wells, so plume "
           "containment is 'preliminary,' and groundwater flows northwest toward the Colorado River. The 2006 UST closure file remains "
           "open with no NFA letter. None of the recommended follow-up (off-site wells, vapor intrusion assessment, VCUP entry, update "
           "before any transaction or financing) has been done in more than five years. The $1.83M-$2.67M estimate is in 2019 dollars "
           "and excludes vapor-intrusion mitigation, off-site remediation, third-party claims and NRD. Only $2.2M of the $3.2M accrual "
           "relates to Grand Junction. As current owner, RES is liable under CERCLA regardless of fault. Because this is an "
           "RCRA-permitted facility, the December 31, 2026 permit renewal could bring facility-wide corrective action. The PLL "
           "policy excludes gradual contamination at owned sites. The Permit Schedule mis-describes the contamination location and "
           "migration direction relative to the Phase II."),
  sources="ESA ss.2-8; EPS s.2.1, s.5; LIT s.VI.A; RPL s.2.1; INS s.4; CAS s.3, s.10",
  exposure="2019 estimate $1.83M-$2.67M; illustrative ~30% cost escalation gives up to ~$3.5M before vapor intrusion, off-site and DNAPL contingencies. Accrual covers $2.2M. Lender EoD if a remediation order exceeds $1M.",
  lo=1830000, hi=3471000,
  impact="Special indemnity; dedicated escrow; price; pre-signing investigation",
  action=("Commission an updated Phase I/II with off-site downgradient wells and a vapor-intrusion assessment (sub-slab and indoor air) "
          "before signing. Address worker exposure immediately. SPA: uncapped or separately capped specific environmental indemnity "
          "for pre-closing conditions at Grand Junction, surviving at least 6 years, backed by a dedicated environmental escrow sized "
          "to the updated estimate. Evaluate VCUP entry and Colorado Petroleum Storage Tank Fund eligibility for the UST release. Bind "
          "a site pollution policy covering known conditions if the market permits."),
  requests="Full 180-page Phase II and the 2018 Phase I; all groundwater monitoring data since 2019; UST closure file; CDPHE correspondence; accrual workpapers."),

 dict(id="ENV-02", cat="Environmental", sev="High",
  title="CDPHE RCRA enforcement (Docket CDPHE-HW-2024-0093): exposure and facts are mischaracterized",
  finding=("The NOV (July 18, 2024) alleges ~14,000 gallons of F001/F002 listed spent solvents were stored in an unpermitted staging area "
           "beyond the 90-day period. The CIM calls it a self-reported 'storage duration exceedance' that is 'within the scope of normal "
           "operations,' and the Permit Schedule describes a satellite-accumulation exceedance of the 55-gallon limit. The parties dispute "
           "12 versus 31 days ($450K versus $1,162,500 at the $37,500/day figure management uses, which is an outdated per-day "
           "maximum). Management's settlement estimate is $200K-$450K, and nothing is accrued. Seller's counsel cites 'no prior RCRA "
           "violations,' while the Permit Schedule notes a 2016 violation. The compliance record will matter for the 2026 Part B renewal. "
           "Post-signing, LOI s.9(e) requires Buyer consent for settlements over $100K."),
  sources="LIT s.III.A; EPS s.2.1, s.6; CIM s.IX.A; LOI s.5.5, s.9(e); CAS s.6, s.12",
  exposure="$200K (management low) to $1.16M+ (CDPHE position), plus possible injunctive/compliance-order costs.",
  lo=200000, hi=1162500,
  impact="Special indemnity; Net Debt/accrual",
  action=("Obtain the NOV, the September 5, 2024 response and the inspection report. Treat the CDPHE penalty as a specific indemnity (or "
          "an indebtedness item at the CDPHE number) outside the basket and cap. Require Buyer approval rights over settlement and over "
          "any compliance order."),
  requests="NOV; inspection report; RES response and exhibits; any CDPHE settlement communications; corrective-action documentation."),

 dict(id="ENV-03", cat="Environmental", sev="High",
  title="Wyoming (Casper) hazardous waste permit expired November 30, 2024; 'timely renewal' status is unverified",
  finding=("Permit WY-HW-2019-033 expired November 30, 2024, and the renewal application was filed October 15, 2024, only 46 days before "
           "expiration. Under the federal RCRA permitting framework generally adopted by authorized states, a renewal application is "
           "due at least 180 days before expiration (40 C.F.R. s.270.10(h)), and continuation of an expired permit depends on a timely "
           "and complete application (s.270.51). Unless Wyoming rules or a DEQ extension provide otherwise, Casper (68 FTEs; Wyoming "
           "revenue $30.2M, or 23.7% of the total) may be operating without valid authorization. Non-renewal of a material permit is "
           "also a credit agreement Event of Default. The CIM describes the filing as timely without qualification."),
  sources="EPS s.2.4; CIM s.III, s.V.C; RPL s.4.3; CCS 'Customer Concentration Summary' (geography); CAS s.10",
  exposure="Interruption or penalties at a facility serving ~$30M of revenue; permit-renewal conditions.",
  lo=None, hi=None,
  impact="Closing condition; special indemnity",
  action=("Obtain the renewal application, DEQ completeness determination and any written confirmation of continued authorization. "
          "Engage Wyoming environmental counsel. Closing condition: renewed permit issued, or written DEQ confirmation that the "
          "facility is authorized to operate pending renewal."),
  requests="Renewal application (Oct 15, 2024); DEQ correspondence; prior permit conditions; 2022 inspection report."),

 dict(id="ENV-04", cat="Environmental", sev="High",
  title="Salt Lake City transfer station permit (UTH-0441) still held by dormant Pinnacle; transfer pending since 2022",
  finding=("The SLC permit remains in the name of Pinnacle Waste Solutions, LLC, which has been dormant since Q3 2022. RES personnel have "
           "operated the facility since March 2022, and Pinnacle's EPA transporter ID was deactivated. The transfer application has been "
           "pending for about 2.75 years, while the Ogden permit was transferred in June 2022. The Permit Schedule acknowledges that "

    r = p.add_run(text); r.font.size = Pt(size); r.bold = bold

    r = p.add_run(text); r.italic = italic
    if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)

def shade(cell, hexcolor):

    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd"); shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def set_cell(cell, text, bold=False, size=9, color=None, align=None):
    cell.text = ""

def table(headers, rows, widths, sevcol=None, size=8.5):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; set_cell(c, h, bold=True, size=size, color=RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)); shade(c, "1F3864")
    # repeat header
    trPr = t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); th.set(qn("w:val"), "true"); trPr.append(th)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            set_cell(cells[i], str(v), size=size)
            if sevcol is not None and i == sevcol and v in SEV_HEX:
                shade(cells[i], SEV_HEX[v])
                cells[i].paragraphs[0].runs[0].bold = True
                if v in ("Critical", "High"):
                    cells[i].paragraphs[0].runs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
    for row in t.rows:
        for i, w in enumerate(widths):
            row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def para(text, bold_lead=None, italic=False, size=None, after=6, style=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if bold_lead:
        r = p.add_run(bold_lead); r.bold = True
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    r = p.add_run(text); r.italic = italic
    if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p

def bullet(text, bold_lead=None, level=0):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet" if level == 0 else "List Bullet 2")
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    if bold_lead:
        r = p.add_run(bold_lead); r.bold = True
    p.add_run(text)
    return p

def numbered(text, bold_lead=None):

    if bold_lead:

# I. Executive Summary and Bottom Line

We have reviewed the 13 documents in the Project Ridgeline data room against the terms of the October 28, 2024 Letter of Intent (the \"LOI\"), under which Sycamore Capital Partners, LP (\"Sycamore\") would acquire Ridgeline Environmental Services, Inc. (\"RES\" or the \"Company\") at an indicative enterprise value of \$182M-\$205M (8.0x-9.0x FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA of \$22.8M), with a 10% holdback, an 18-month general survival period, and a target signing date of February 14, 2025.

**Bottom line:** We do not recommend proceeding to a signed SPA on the LOI terms. The data room does not yet support the earnings, revenue base or regulatory standing on which the price rests. Seven issues are critical. (1) The Adjusted EBITDA bridge does not reconcile. (2) A \$1.2M litigation \'cost\' add-back appears to be a \$1.2M gain. (3) Earnings fell about 15% in FY2024. (4) Audit status is contradictory. (5) DOE revenue (19.2% of the total) is about twice what the IDIQ task orders support, and the contract ceiling runs out in early-to-mid 2025. (6) The data room contains two irreconcilable customer lists. (7) Grand Junction headquarters has uninsured, uninvestigated chlorinated-solvent contamination with a potential vapor-intrusion pathway into an occupied building. On our illustrative base case, diligence-adjusted EBITDA is approximately \$21.2M (EV \$169M-\$190M, or \$12.8M-\$14.7M below the LOI range). In a downside case it is \$19.0M (EV \$152M-\$171M). If the DOE ceiling is not increased, run-rate EBITDA could fall toward \~\$16.7M. Quantified contingent and debt-like exposures not in the LOI price mechanics total roughly \$7.0M-\$20.4M before unquantified items. The high end is about equal to the entire proposed 10% holdback, which also serves as the general indemnity cap.

These issues are not necessarily fatal. Most can be addressed through a re-based price, specific (special) indemnities with dedicated escrows, closing conditions and pre-signing deliverables, as set out in Section VII. But several, especially REV-01, REV-02, FIN-02 and FIN-05, go to the integrity of management\'s financial reporting. I've written both deliverables, the red-flag memo and a companion tracker. Both open cleanly, the skill validators passed on both, and the workbook has no formula errors after recalculation. I read all 13 data room documents in full through `sbx.sh`/`parse-doc` and did not open `task.json`, the rubric or anything else on the host apart from the brief.

**Bottom line of the memo:** don't sign on the LOI terms (EV $182M–$205M, 8.0x–9.0x on $22.8M Adjusted EBITDA). The review produced 35 red flags: 7 Critical, 15 High, 12 Medium and 1 Low.

**The 7 Critical issues:**
- **EBITDA doesn't reconcile.** The CIM says $22.8M and the QoE bridge says $23.8M, with $1.0M unexplained. The $18.4M management calls "reported EBITDA" is actually EBIT in the QoE profit and loss.
- **The $1.2M litigation "cost" add-back is likely a gain.** The QoE says RES paid $1.2M to settle the Harper case, but seller's counsel says Harper is still pending and the $1.2M was a payment *to* RES from Clearwater.
- **Earnings are falling.** Adjusted EBITDA dropped from $28.1M in FY2023 to $23.8M in FY2024, and the CIM leaves out historical EBITDA.
- **Audit status is contradictory.** One document says never audited, another says audited, another refers to FY2024 audited statements. The LOI makes audits a closing condition and the credit agreement requires them.
- **DOE contract (19.2% of revenue).** Reported DOE revenue of $63.9M is about twice the $31.7M recognized under the task orders and exceeds the $45M contract ceiling. The ceiling runs out around April–May 2025, possibly sooner: remaining ceiling may be ~$6.8M rather than $12.3M. That is a revenue hit of at least $12.1M.
- **Two different customer lists.** The customer schedule and the QoE share only two of their top-20 customers, yet both total $127.3M.
- **Grand Junction HQ contamination.** It is uninsured and has not been investigated since 2019. A potential vapor-intrusion pathway runs into a building occupied daily by employees.

**Other key High findings:**
- **Permits.** The Wyoming (Casper) permit expired after a renewal filed only 46 days before expiry. The Salt Lake City permit is still in the name of the dormant Pinnacle subsidiary.
- **Salt Lake City lease.** RES has never obtained the landlord's consent since acquiring Pinnacle in 2022, which is likely an existing default.
- **Workforce.** A union election petition was filed November 4, 2024, disclosed only in a footnote. About 148 employees hold HAZWOPER certification, against roughly 310 field personnel the CIM claims are all certified.
- **Liabilities and payouts.**
  - Asbestos tail exposure is largely uninsured, and two open asbestos workers' comp claims were not disclosed.
  - Change-of-control severance totals $3.775M, of which $2.625M to the founders is single-trigger.
  - The 401(k) safe-harbor match was suspended for six months in 2023.
  - Fleet replacement backlog is $9.8M.
  - The CDPHE penalty exposure runs from $200K to $1.16M.

**Valuation figures:** these are illustrative estimates for negotiation, not valuations.
